original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-efface-cohomology-on-closed-by-finite-cover}
Let $X$ be an affine scheme. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a torsion abelian sheaf
on  $X_\etale$. Let $Z \subset X$ be a closed subscheme. Let
$\xi \in H^q_\etale(Z, \mathcal{F}|_Z)$ for some $q > 0$.
Then there exists an injective map $\mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{F}'$
of torsion abelian sheaves on $X_\etale$ such that
the image of $\xi$ in $H^q_\etale(Z, \mathcal{F}'|_Z)$ is zero.

final_content.statement:
A geometric point of a scheme is a morphism $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ with algebraically closed $\Omega$; its étale stalk is a filtered colimit over pointed étale neighborhoods. A *strictly henselian local ring* is henselian with separably closed residue field. $H^q_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X,\mathcal F)$ means right-derived global sections of an **abelian sheaf** $\mathcal F$ on the small étale site; ordinary global sections $\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)$ also make sense for sheaves of sets. A *henselian pair* $(A,I)$ is a ring and ideal satisfying the standard lifting property for idempotents and appropriate polynomial factorizations modulo $I$; write $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $Z=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$. A *spectral space* is quasi-compact and sober with a basis of quasi-compact opens closed under finite intersection. A sheaf of rings is *torsion* when its underlying additive-group stalks are torsion; an injective module sheaf is injective in the corresponding abelian category of module sheaves, not necessarily injective as a sheaf of sets.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-h0-henselian-pair}
Let $(A, I)$ be a henselian pair. Set $X = \Spec(A)$ and
$Z = \Spec(A/I)$. For any sheaf $\mathcal{F}$ on $X_\etale$
we have $\Gamma(X, \mathcal{F}) = \Gamma(Z, \mathcal{F}|_Z)$.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-vanishing-restriction-injective}
Let $X$ be a scheme with affine diagonal which can be covered by
$n + 1$ affine opens. Let $Z \subset X$ be a closed subscheme.
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be a torsion sheaf of rings on $X_\etale$
and let $\mathcal{I}$ be an injective sheaf of $\mathcal{A}$-modules
on $X_\etale$.
Then $H^q_\etale(Z, \mathcal{I}|_Z) = 0$ for $q > n$.
